title: Well Designed, Light, Convenient, not the best on heavily soiled carpets
text: Well Designed, Light, Convenient, not the best on heavily soiled carpets. I have mixed feelings about this carpet cleaner.  I am spoiled by having used a Rug Doctor, which really does an excellent job.  My old Rug Doctor is on its last legs, so thought I would give this cleaner a try.  I had bought a Bissell carpet cleaner several years ago, but ended up returning it as it didn't work that well.  Thought I would try again as I assumed that improvements had been made over the years.  It does seem like it is a better machine than the one from several years ago and it really seemed to get a lot of dirt out of the carpet and pulled out a lot of lint too.  I would classify it as an adequate cleaner if your carpets are not heavily soiled.  It didn't work as well as my Rug Doctor to get out ground in dirt, but when you consider that it is 1/2 to a 1/3 of the price of a Rug Doctor, it does a lot for the price.  I like the idea that the tank you fill will hot water comes out and you can take it to the sink and leave the machine plugged in and not have to move it.  With my Rug Doctor, every time I need to fill the water, I have to unplug it and take the whole machine to the sink, dump the dirty water and fill it with clean water from a pitcher.  With the Bissell, you just run the water directly from the faucet into the tank.  The power cord is a reasonable length.  It's long enough so you don't have to move the machine too often, but short enough not to get in the way.  The machine is light and easy to manuveur. Rug Doctor uses one backwards pass to clean.  The Bissell uses one forward and one backward pass dispensing cleaning solution and then a foward and backward pass to vacuum up the water.  It's 4 passes instead of one, but the machine is not that heavy so it's not a big deal to make the 4 passes.  I liked the hand attachment that you use with the built-in hose; it worked very well.  The machine noise is about normal for a carpet cleaner, approximately like a vacuum cleaner.  Very easy to assemble the machine; just a few screws.  So what's wrong with this machine?  On heavily soiled carpets, it seemed to leave a lot of streaks and put out too much soapy mixture.  It's possible I used too much cleaning solution as the small included bottle said double strength, but I used the included measuring cup, so I assumed it was the right amount.  I also had a hard time figuring out how the built-in hose was supposed to wrap around; there is no picture or diagram.  My sister figured it out right away how to do it, so chalk that up to my being a dummy.  The biggest issue I had with this machine is that when you turn it off and start to move it, it drips a lot of water out and can spot up the carpet; then you have to run it again over the spots and they don't come out easily.  I also noticed that the restricted area that sucks up the water is narrow enough that lint accumulates and requires cleaning just about after each use.  This is a decent machine for the money and I would give it a solid 3 stars; maybe 3 1/2.  If you don't have a lot of very dirty carpet, this might be perfect for you.  It beats paying double or triple the price for a more heavy duty machine, unless you need the heavier duty cleaning power.  If you clean your carpet regularly, this should do the job just fine.  If you have a lot of dirt and have pets, this might not quite do the job, unless you use it often.
